headline: High-risk write-capable ECC can conflict with and cascade from a read-only awesome-nlp peer; prompt-injection and leakage are limited by the pair’s lack of shared channels.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-nlp is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, while ECC has stdin/stdout, files, and MCP. A direct injection path is not documented, but if a user manually copies awesome-nlp content into ECC skills or prompts, ECC could treat it as instructions. The pair lacks a built-in shared channel, so this stays low.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies awesome-nlp content into ECC prompts, skills, or MCP inputs
IF ECC parses copied text as instructions rather than inert content
mitigations: Keep awesome-nlp outputs out of ECC prompt text
Paste only quoted excerpts with explicit delimiters
Disable MCP inputs for untrusted copied content
Review any imported skill or rule text before enabling it

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-nlp touches no data classes and has no network egress, while ECC can read/write local files and call APIs. There is no documented shared workspace between them, so leakage is limited to unusual operator setup such as copying files into ECC-managed paths. The pair does not show a default sensitive-data flow.
conditions: IF the operator places sensitive files into ECC-accessible directories
IF ECC uploads those files through its allowlisted API calls
mitigations: Do not place sensitive files in ECC-managed folders
Use a separate workspace for ECC runs
Audit which files ECC reads before execution
Restrict allowlisted API destinations to approved tenants

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-nlp has no write or execution capabilities, but ECC can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses. The pair therefore has asymmetric overlap on shared local resources if co-located, and ECC’s concurrency notes warn about separate roots to avoid overwriting session files. Uncertainty about the exact deployment pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same working directory
IF ECC session files or git state are shared across runs
mitigations: Use separate roots for ECC and any other agent
Avoid concurrent git operations in the same repo
Check ECC session-path settings before launch

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-nlp is a curated list, so its content can be treated as authoritative by ECC if copied into rules, skills, or prompts. ECC’s skills-first workflow and subagent delegation increase the chance that unverified upstream content becomes downstream action material. Because no direct interaction is documented, this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF awesome-nlp content is imported into ECC rules, skills, or prompts
IF ECC acts on that imported content without verification
mitigations: Require a verification step before ECC acts on imported content
Mark imported list items as non-authoritative
Separate reference material from executable rules
Have a human approve any action derived from copied content

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class is identified for awesome-nlp, and ECC’s listed data classes are operational metadata, code, and documentation rather than regulated personal data. The profiles do not show a residency, retention, or certification mismatch for the pair, so no compliance breach pathway is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is introduced into ECC workflows
IF a separate policy requires controls not shown in either profile
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of this pair
Review retention settings before storing session data
Document any policy exceptions before deployment
